Kate (Acme): Hey support, we started seeing requests from our mobile app routed to us-east even though the app sends region header 'eu-west-1'. Can we escalate?
maya_support: Hi Kate — can you paste raw request headers (curl or HAR)?
Kate (Acme): Here's a curl dump:
`````
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -H "X-Client-Region: еu-west-1" https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
`````
jonah_eng_oncall: FYI that 'e' in your header looks... off. Can you run a hexdump or quick python check of the header value?
Kate (Acme): Ran quick python check:
`````
>>> s = 'еu-west-1'
>>> [hex(ord(c)) for c in s]
['0xd0', '0xb5', '0x75', '0x2d', '0x77', '0x65', '0x73', '0x74', '0x2d', '0x31']
`````
maya_support: Oof — that's Cyrillic small 'ie' (U+0435) at the start, not ASCII 'e'. Router does an ASCII mapping so it doesn't match our 'eu-west-1' key. Falls back to nearest POP.
jonah_eng_oncall: Reproduced in edge logs: parsed_region="еu-west-1" -> no mapping -> fallback to closest region (us-west-2). Explains cross-region latency and billing discrepancy.
sam_sre: Short-term mitigation: I'll push an edge filter to normalize incoming region headers (NFKC + strip non-ascii) at 15:20 UTC. Long-term: add explicit unicode-normalize + ascii-whitelist in router.
Kate (Acme): Thanks — is there something we can do on our side to avoid this entirely? Users copy/pasting from docs/PDFs all the time.
maya_support: Recommend client-side validation: e.g. in Python: `import unicodedata; clean = unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', region).encode('ascii','ignore').decode()` before sending headers. We'll also add an SDK validator and a note in the quickstart.
jonah_eng_oncall: infra-bot: canary deploy of edge normalizer started 15:28 UTC.
infra-bot: canary deploy successful to 3 EU POPs (canary-id: cn-7382). No errors in health checks.
jonah_eng_oncall: Please verify after ~15:35 UTC and report if you still see misroutes. :thumbsup:
Kate (Acme): Verified at 15:40 UTC — requests now hit EU POP. Thanks everyone! :tada:
